issues.reason: *Existential* states flatly that "Indefinite 'a/an' is generic in a copular / definitional predication (\"A dog is a mammal\" = (Inheritance dog mammal))", and this is exactly such a clause, so minting sk_lantern_1 and asserting (Member sk_lantern_1 heavy) / (Member sk_lantern_1 stone_construction) puts a particular existing lantern and its properties into the KB where the text makes only a kind-level claim.

gaps_confirmed: generic copular claim whose subject is a proper-noun-premodified head ("a Cliff Path lantern is ..."): the copular generic needs a kind symbol on the left of Inheritance, but the proper-noun-premodifier rule bars fusing name + head into one kind and links them by Possession instead
new_gaps: the *Conditional properties* extension that puts a restricting place in the condition slot ("rents are steep in the capital") is stated for a locative / domain PP only, so it is not clearly available to carry a proper-noun PREMODIFIER's restriction on a generic kind subject — leaving the restriction with no stated carrier and no way to state the generic without dropping it
defect_summary: The compliant form is a kind-level generic that keeps the Cliff-Path restriction — the nearest licensed analogue being the condition slot of *Conditional properties*, (ConditionalProperty lantern heavy cliff_path) + (ConditionalProperty lantern stone_construction cliff_path) alongside the unchanged (Name cliff_path "Cliff Path"), (Member cliff_path path) and (Inheritance stone_construction construction); if that analogue is rejected as PP-only then NO kind-level form is licensed for this subject shape, and the claim would have to be left out with the gap recorded, since a bare (Inheritance lantern heavy) silently drops the stated restriction and so is barred by *Core patterns*.
notes: Only the generic-vs-witness routing fails: the Northgate-spokesman treatment of the premodifier, the type atom licensed by the kind word inside "Cliff Path", and the heavy / stone_construction split (incidental description separate, material-noun compound fused with head genus only) are all correct.
